extracted.intended_audience: US and foreign patent counsel and IP practitioners handling design patents and Hague (IDA) filings
extracted.subtask_short: US design patent and Hague IDA practice
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing, filing, prosecuting and managing international design applications (IDAs) under the Hague Agreement as they affect US design patent practice, including eligibility, formalities, national examination, US-specific rules and prosecution strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicants Entitled to Use the Hague System
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant can file an IDA using the Hague System only if it meets at least one entitlement criterion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entitlement criteria: national of a Contracting Party (or member state of an intergovernmental organization that is a Contracting Party, e.g., EU or OAPI); domiciled in a Contracting Party's territory; has a real and effective industrial or commercial establishment in a Contracting Party's territory. Under the Geneva Act, habitual residence in a Contracting Party also qualifies (taken from Berne Convention to compensate for narrow 'domicile').

rubrics_metrics.name: Languages in which an IDA must be filed
rubrics_metrics.description: The IDA must be filed in English, French or Spanish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File the international design application in one of WIPO's accepted languages to meet IB formal requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDA Must Include a Reproduction of the Industrial Design
rubrics_metrics.description: The IDA must include a reproduction of the industrial design the applicant seeks to protect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare a single set of reproductions for all designated Contracting Parties; reproductions should meet WIPO publication/image quality standards and each designated Contracting Party's specific requirements (e.g., acceptance of partial designs or shaded/unshaded figures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum Number of Designs per IDA and Locarno Classification Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: An IDA may include up to 100 different designs only if the designs all belong to the same International Classification (Locarno Classification).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify all designs fall within the same Locarno class/subclass before grouping them in one IDA; the Locarno Classification is available on WIPO's website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two Filing Routes to Access the Hague System
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants can access the Hague System either by filing directly with WIPO's International Bureau (IB) or by indirect filing with their home patent office (e.g., USPTO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct filing requires payment to WIPO and adherence to IB procedures; indirect filing (e.g., via USPTO) requires following national office rules (entitlement checks, forwarding fee, national security review) and may affect the filing date rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees and Fee Payment Rules for IDAs
rubrics_metrics.description: When filing directly in the IB, applicants must pay in Swiss francs the basic filing fee, the publication fee, and a fee for each designated Contracting Party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees generally payable on filing unless applicant requests deferment of publication (then pay later per Common Regulations, Rule 12(2)). When designating the US, part of the designation fee is paid at filing and the rest at allowance (Rule 12(3)); that two-part fee covers maintenance for the design patent's entire 15-year term (37 C.F.R. § 1.1031(e)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of Contracting Parties and Reproductions Strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Country selection and the single set of drawings should be based on a strategy to maximize design rights across designated Contracting Parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider each Contracting Party's IP rights regime (e.g., acceptance of partial designs, shaded/unshaded figures), strength of IP enforcement, where the product will be sold, likelihood of copying, and prosecution/examination cost. Also address each designated Contracting Party's reproduction requirements before filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic Extent of Protection is Limited to Contracting Parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Design protection under the Hague System is available only in the Contracting Parties to the particular Act used by the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the Geneva, Hague and London Acts are independent, protection is limited to Contracting Parties of the specific Act under which the IDA was filed; the US is party only to the Geneva Act so US applicants get protection only in Geneva Act Contracting Parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign Filing License Requirement for US Applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: US applicants must obtain a foreign filing license before filing an application in a foreign country for an invention made in the US, which includes filing an IDA with the IB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain a foreign filing license under 35 U.S.C. § 184 or submit a petition under 37 C.F.R. § 5.12 or § 5.13 to avoid fines and penalties for unauthorized foreign filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO's Role When Acting as an Indirect Filing Office
rubrics_metrics.description: When a US applicant files an IDA with the USPTO (indirect filing), the USPTO determines entitlement, ensures payment of the forwarding fee, conducts a national security review, and forwards the IDA to the IB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO does not conduct the IB's formalities review; timing rules apply for the filing date depending on when the IB receives the forwarded IDA (see Common Regulations, Rules 13(3)(i) and (4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: IDA Filing Date Rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The IDA's filing date is generally the date the IB receives the IDA, unless there is an irregularity; for USPTO-filed IDAs the filing date may be the USPTO receive date if the IB receives the IDA within certain time limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Irregularities can change the effective international registration date; follow Common Regulations for timing consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: International Formalities Review by the IB
rubrics_metrics.description: The IB conducts a formalities review (not a substantive merits examination) to confirm the IDA meets formal requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IB formalities checks include that the design image reproduction quality is consistent with WIPO publication standards (Common Regulations, Rule 9) and that the applicant has included prescribed data and filing fees (Rule 7). If formalities are met, IB registers the design and publishes it (usually six months after registration date).

rubrics_metrics.name: Invitation to Correct Certain Irregularities and Timing
rubrics_metrics.description: If the IDA lacks required content, the IB issues an Invitation to Correct Certain Irregularities; the applicant typically has three months to comply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Common Regulations, Rule 14(1) for timing; failure to respond can affect registration and rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication Options and Timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The IB publishes the design six months after the international registration date, but the applicant may request immediate publication or a delay (subject to country restrictions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediate publication may maximize provisional rights; delay might avoid premature public disclosure (but when designating the US, deferment of publication is not permitted).

rubrics_metrics.name: National Examination vs Non-examination Systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Design protection depends on the national regime: substantive examination systems conduct merits review (novelty, non-obviousness), while non-examination systems conduct only formalities review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In substantive systems (e.g., the US) a design is reviewed against prior art for novelty and non-obviousness and, if allowed, is enforceable; in non-examination systems, third parties must challenge validity post-grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: No Automatic Grant of US Protection from an IDA
rubrics_metrics.description: Although international registration can have effect in some non-examining Contracting Parties, the Hague Agreement permits a Contracting Party to refuse protection; US law requires a separate US design patent grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under US law (35 U.S.C. §§ 151 and 389(d); 37 C.F.R. § 1.1071), the USPTO cannot grant US design patent protection solely by virtue of WIPO registration; the USPTO examines and may refuse protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority Rights — Domestic and Foreign
rubrics_metrics.description: A US-designated IDA may serve as a priority national application for later US continuations/divisionals (35 U.S.C. § 120); foreign priority (six-month Paris Convention) still applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An IDA is entitled to a right of priority from previously filed foreign application, a PCT application designating at least one country other than the US (35 U.S.C. § 351(c)), or an IDA designating other countries. Use these rules to perfect priority claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional Rights from Publication of a US-designated IDA
rubrics_metrics.description: Since May 13, 2015, design patent owners may have provisional rights from publication of a US-designated IDA that can entitle a reasonable royalty for infringing acts between publication and issue date where the issued design is substantially similar to the published IDA (35 U.S.C. § 154(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh provisional rights benefits against the drawback that publication of the IDA can make US priority applications publicly available (37 C.F.R. § 1.14) whereas US non-provisional design applications are usually kept secret until grant (35 U.S.C § 122(b)(2)(A)(iv)).

rubrics_metrics.name: US Special Rules of Practice for US-designated IDAs
rubrics_metrics.description: IDAs that designate the US must comply with specific US rules under 37 C.F.R. §§ 1.1001–1.1071.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key US requirements: include a specification and a claim; claim language must fit US design law (see 37 C.F.R. §§ 1.1024 and 1.1025); IDAs designating the US can include no more than one claim directed to only one independent and distinct design (37 C.F.R. §§ 1.1025 and 1.1064); cannot request deferment of publication when designating the US (37 C.F.R. § 1.1028); must include an oath or declaration for US filing (37 C.F.R. § 1.1021(d)(3) and § 1.1067(b)); corrections by IB must be sent to USPTO before applicable (37 C.F.R. § 1.1065).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim Language Form Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim language must be in the form of an 'ornamental design' of the subject article 'as shown' or 'as shown and described' for US-designated IDAs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft the claim to conform to the specified formulation (37 C.F.R. § 1.1025) to avoid formal defects and ensure compatibility with US design practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of Design / Single Design Invention Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: US law continues to focus on a single design invention; while multiple embodiments of the same inventive concept are allowed, disclosing more than one patentably distinct design can trigger a restriction requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a restriction is issued, the applicant must select one design or file divisional applications for non-elected designs (35 U.S.C. § 121); expect potential additional fees and prosecution of multiple divisional applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited Examination Eligibility and Procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Expedited examination is available to design applicants who meet certain conditions and can result in a US design patent in as little as 60 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements: conduct a preliminary examination search; file an information disclosure statement (IDS), proper drawings and a request for expedited treatment; pay the required fee (37 C.F.R. § 1.155). For US-designated IDAs, expedited examination is available only after WIPO publication and upon request to the USPTO by local US patent counsel (37 C.F.R. § 1.155(a)(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty of Disclosure and Use of Information Disclosure Statements (IDS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Anyone associated with filing/prosecution must deal with the USPTO with candor and in good faith, including a duty to disclose information material to patentability (37 C.F.R. § 1.56); an IDS is the common mechanism for disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IDS may be filed at the time the IDA is filed using a WIPO prescribed form or with the USPTO within three months after WIPO publishes the IDA (37 C.F.R. § 1.97(b)); some fees may apply. US patent counsel should typically file the IDS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor Oath or Declaration Requirements and Flexibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: AIA changes permit various flexibilities in inventor oath/declaration practice for design applications filed directly in the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted practices include assignee filing the oath/declaration as applicant; postponing filing until the application is in condition for allowance; reusing a previously signed oath/declaration; providing substitute oaths/declarations if inventor is deceased, incapacitated, refuses to sign, or cannot be located; and making the oath/declaration in an inventor's assignment form (37 C.F.R. §§ 1.63 and 1.64). For US-designated IDAs the IB performs a formal review and the WIPO-prescribed oath/declaration should be filed (Annex I to DM/1 and 37 C.F.R. § 1.1021(d) and § 1.1067).

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for US Counsel for US-designated IDAs
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign applicants must engage US patent counsel when an IDA designates the US because the USPTO substantively examines design patent applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: US counsel is needed to respond to USPTO office actions, perfect foreign priority and file documents such as IDSs after WIPO publishes the IDA. If a signed oath/declaration isn't filed, IB may delete the US designation and US rights may be abandoned (Geneva Act, Art. 8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ownership and Assignment Recording to Perfect US Rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Under US law, inventors own the invention unless they assign rights; assignees should record assignment with the USPTO to perfect ownership and enable enforcement in the assignee's name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recording an assignment in the USPTO: perfects transfer, provides proof for filing terminal disclaimers to overcome obviousness-type double patenting rejections, ensures the USPTO issues the patent in the assignee's name. Changes recorded in the International Register (WIPO) are not effective in the US for some partial changes (Common Regulations Rule 21(7); 37 C.F.R. § 1.1065(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of AIA (FITF) and Post-Grant Challenges to IDAs
rubrics_metrics.description: IDAs designating the US are examined under the Leahy-Smith America Invents Act's first-inventor-to-file (FITF) provisions and are subject to post-grant and inter partes review proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat IDAs like regularly filed US design patent applications for purposes of AIA changes and available USPTO post-grant challenge procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: US Design Patent Term
rubrics_metrics.description: Design patent term increased from 14 years to 15 years from issuance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 35 U.S.C. § 173; the two-part designation fee paid to WIPO for US designation covers the patent's entire 15-year term (37 C.F.R. § 1.1031(e)).

rubrics_metrics.name: IB Corrections/Changes Must Be Communicated to USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: Any correction or change in an IDA by the IB must also be sent to the USPTO before the change is applicable to the US application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow 37 C.F.R. § 1.1065 to ensure US records reflect IB corrections; failure to do so can affect US rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO Timing to Communicate a Reason for Refusal to WIPO
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO has 12 months from publication of the IDA (rather than the standard six months) to communicate any reason of refusal to WIPO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 C.F.R. § 1.1062(b); plan prosecution and responses accordingly given the extended communication window.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO May Refuse to Transmit IDA for National Security Reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO may refuse to transmit an IDA to the IB if transmission threatens national security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 C.F.R. § 1.1002(b)(4); applicants should be aware of potential national security reviews when filing indirectly via USPTO.
